title: Public Safety Through Food Access Act
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill allows North Carolina to remove federal restrictions that prevent individuals convicted of drug-related felonies from receiving food assistance and temporary aid benefits. Instead of permanent disqualification, eligible individuals could receive benefits after either completing substance abuse treatment in prison or six months after conviction without committing additional drug offenses, provided they participate in required treatment programs.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill promotes public safety and successful reentry by helping formerly incarcerated individuals meet basic needs like food, which reduces barriers to employment and stable housing. They contend that access to assistance combined with mandatory substance abuse treatment addresses root causes of recidivism and helps individuals rebuild productive lives in their communities.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue that removing restrictions could be seen as insufficiently punitive toward drug felony convictions and question whether mandatory treatment requirements are adequately enforceable or funded. Some may also express concerns about the fiscal cost of expanding benefit eligibility and whether resources should prioritize other populations in need.
